NIDHI GUPTA, J.

Present appeal has been filed by the claimant seeking enhancement of compensation of Rs.25,34,524 Rs.25,34,524/- awarded by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Jhajjar (hereinafter referred to as "the Tribunal"), vide Award dated 29.10.2024 passed in MACP MACP-270-2019 dated 07.09.2019 filed under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act (hereinafter "the Act").
The sole claimant is the mother of deceased Sachin son of Om Parkash.
2. Brief facts of the case as pleaded in the claim petition are that on 07.05.2019, there was marriage of Vishal (brother of deceased Sachin) at Beri.

Beri After attending marriage ceremony in the n night ight of 07/08.05.2019, Sachin along with Satish, Subham, Devender and Yogesh were coming back to village Mehrana in Swift Car No.DL No.DL-1CN-9054 (hereinafter referred to as "the accidental vehicle") being driven by Yogesh.

The driver of accidental vehicle could not see the offending vehicle and therefore, the accidental vehicle struck into the offending vehicle from back side.

sentences.text: As has already been noted above, it has been admitted by the claimant in the claim petition that the accident in question took place as the accidental ve vehicle in which the deceased was travelling had struck into the offending vehicle from the back.
9. Further, claimants had pr produced Middle Standard Examination Certificate of deceased (Ex.P4), in which his date of birth is mentioned as 30.10.1992.
Thus, age of the deceased at the time of accident was 27 years 5 days.
Respondents have not produced any evidence rebutting the age of of deceased.

Income of deceased was also proved to be Rs.17,258/-
Rs.17,258/ per month at the time of his death.
10. The appellant has sought enhancement only under the conventional heads.

However, the Hon'ble Supreme Court in (SC) SLP No.13931 of 2017 titled as "New India Assurance Co. Ltd. Vs.
Vinish Jain & Others" Law Finder Doc ID # 977386, 977386 it has been held that where difference in compensation is about 4 to 5 per cent only, it does not warrant interference by this Court as, such variation in compensation is within ithin permissible limits.

It is trite law that the Tribunal is permitted to do some guess work and also exercise its discretion to fix the reasonable and just compensation, for which there cannot be any straitjacket formula based on mathematical precision.

In New India Assurance Company Vs. Vinish Jain and Others [(2018) 3 SCC 619], the Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that if the fixation of compensation is within permissible limits, the courts should normally not interfere with such awards".

The other area of dispute is that the Tribunal after awarding compensation under the conventional heads has awarded Rs.75,000/-
Rs.75,000/ towards loss of love and affection and Rs.10,000/ awarded towards pain and sufferings.
In New India Assurance Co., Ltd v. Vineesh.J[2018 (3) SCC 619], the Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that the Appellate Court can permit variation of plus or minus 4 to 5 percent."

sentences.text: 13. From the above facts, it is clear that a very just and fair compensation has been awarded to the appellant.
Nothing whatsoever has been shown to this Court that would m merit enhancement of the compensation granted to the appellant.
Accordingly, I find no case is made out which merits interference with the impugned Award.
I find the compensation awarded to the appellant to be just and fair in the facts and circumstances of the case.

No doubt Chapter Chapter-12 of the Act is a beneficial legislation yet, as cautioned by the Hon'ble Supreme Court, the same 5 of 6 Neutral Citation No:=2025:PHHC:057186 cannot be allowed to be treated as a windfall or a source of profit.

Hon'ble 'State of Haryana & Another Vs. Jas Supreme Court in 'State Jasbir Kaur & Others' Law Finder Doc ID # 64043 and 'Divisional Controller K.S.R.T.C. Vs. Mahadev Shetty', (2003) 7 SCC 197, has held that the amount of compensation should be just and reasonable, it should neither be a bonanza nor a source of profit but at the the same time it should not be a pittance.

sentences.text: Thus, all that has to be determined in the facts of a given case is, that the compensation accorded is 'just'.

In my considered view, in the present case, the learned Tribunal has awarded a very 'just' compensation,
which is in accordance with the law laid down by the compensation, Hon'ble Supreme Court and therefore, does not warrant the interference of this Court.

In the case of "General Manager, KSRTC Vs. Susamma Thomas & Others" 1994 Volume-II Volume II SCC 176, the Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that misplaced sympathy, generosity and benevolence cannot be the guiding factor for determining the compensation.
